name: Ogwen 15K
start: Plas y Brenin; confirm wave time.
course: Gallt yr Ogof, Cefn y Capel ridge and Foel Goch before returning to Capel Curig.
transport: Mountain centre start and finish; check parking and early arrival
facilities: Event support and final instructions published close to race day
rules: Mountain terrain needs appropriate kit and weather judgment; check final kit list.
reason: Only 15K, but nearly 700m ascent and exposed terrain make it a mountain race. It is a better short-route comparison for fell runners than road 10Ks.

name: Ogwen 40K
start: Plas y Brenin; start time to check in final pack.
course: Glyderau and Carneddau ridges with Grade 1 scrambling.
transport: Start and finish at Plas y Brenin; confirm parking and support access
facilities: Check route-specific aid and mandatory kit
rules: Experienced mountain movement and scrambling are relevant; verify event qualification and cut-offs.
reason: The 40K crosses two mountain ranges, with more than 2,400m climbing and scrambling. It requires very different experience from the shorter Ogwen options.

name: Trail 10K Eryri
start: Llanberis; exact wave time to confirm.
course: Hillside trails and Dinorwig Quarry after about 6.5km.
transport: Llanberis start and finish; check July event parking
facilities: Two on-course support points, event village and timing
rules: Course measures 9.8km despite 10K name; choose trail shoes for climbing and descent.
reason: A short mountain course with around 400m ascent and a quarry section. Its 9.8km measured route is unlike a flat road 10K.

name: Brecon Beacons Trails
start: 51K 08:00; 24K time conflicts on organiser page, confirm.
course: Moorland, forest trails and exposed mountain ridges from Talybont.
transport: Henderson Hall event hub; paid parking on site
facilities: Bag drop, venue toilets and course aid stations
rules: Minimum age 20 for 51K and 17 for 24K; carry GPX for backup navigation.
reason: Technical mountain trails with a 51K checkpoint timetable. The organiser page conflicts on the 24K start time, so that must be confirmed before travel.

name: Rabbit Run Wales
course: The 12K includes trails, a river crossing and Big Dipper dune; longer routes reach Glamorgan coast.
transport: Merthyr Mawr Estate event site; confirm parking and camping arrangements
facilities: Family races and event-weekend camping option
rules: The 2027 edition has no ultra distance; confirm route and river conditions.
reason: Sand dune and river crossing make even the 12K unusually varied. The 2027 half is new, while the former ultra is absent, so choose the current edition carefully.

name: Chasewater Trail Festival
course: Grass, lakeside paths and woodland: half four laps plus spur, 10K two, 5K one.
transport: Country-park parking is paid and closes at 15:00; nearest bus stop about 18 minutes on foot
facilities: Informal bag drop, village toilets and water for 10K and half
rules: Not suitable for wheelchairs or prams; 5K has no course water.
reason: Mixed terrain and separate start times matter more than the short published climbing figures. The 5K lacks on-course water, and parking closes at 15:00.
